question: When ceritinib used instead of crizotinib?

supports.item: patients who are intolerant to crizotinib
supports.quote: Ceritinib is approved for the treatment of ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC in patients who are intolerant to or have progressed despite therapy with crizotinib.

supports.item: patients who have progressed despite therapy with crizotinib
supports.quote: Ceritinib is approved for the treatment of ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC in patients who are intolerant to or have progressed despite therapy with crizotinib.
Ceritinib is a second-generation ALK inhibitor that has demonstrated activity in crizotinib-resistant patients, becoming a promising treatment option in this population.

supports.item: ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC patients with crizotinib resistance
supports.quote: Altogether, our results demonstrate that ceritinib can overcome crizotinib resistance, consistent with clinical data showing marked efficacy of ceritinib in patients with crizotinib-resistant disease.

initial_executor.limitations: Evidence indicates ceritinib is used for ALK-positive NSCLC patients who are intolerant to or have progressed on crizotinib. However, ceritinib does not overcome all crizotinib-resistant ALK mutations, specifically G1202R and F1174C (e9, e10). The evidence does not support use as a first-line alternative for crizotinib-naïve patients despite mentioning activity in such populations (e3), as approval is specifically tied to intolerance or progression.
